idiom_name: Slick Table classes with mapped projections plus a sealed-trait hierarchy and match dispatch
implementation_notes: Scala ORMs do not map inheritance: Slick defines one Table class per table with a mapped projection ('<>' or mapTo) onto a case class, and the domain hierarchy is a sealed trait with case-class variants, so the mapper is an explicit function that reads the discriminator (an sti key column) and returns the right variant - or joins the subclass table when the schema is class-table shaped. Abstract mapping behaviour is shared through a trait, per-class behaviour through each Table's projection, and inheritance in the domain does not carry over into the mappers.
pitfalls: Extending a Table class and overriding '*' does not compose the way class inheritance does - Slick returns the row type of the projection, so inheritance stops at the case class.
Slick has no lazy loading: navigational access must be written as explicit joins, otherwise a 'mapper' turns into N queries per row.
DBIO actions are descriptions: a mapper that builds a query must be sequenced by the caller, or nothing runs and the bug looks like an empty result.
